title: Prove the logged clause in the proof checker's SMT fallback
summary: The proof checker's SMT fallback now refutes the negation of the logged clause on its own, and uses a plugin's simplified condition only when the logged clause follows from the hint's clause by subsumption plus RUP, closing a hole where any logged clause passed under a tautological hint. The checker also reports failure to its callers and prints the 'is not rup' diagnostic only on rejected steps.
